label: miso21 cc border anchor
definition: Two measured-grounded structural levers on top of miso18 (export cap retained). LEVER 1 -- cc_intermediate_split: MISO's combined-cycle fleet runs baseload (measured CAMPD median CF 50-150 %; all 39 CC plants clear the threshold), yet inherited the CC_REGULAR offer curve shaped for ERCOT duct-fire-heavy peaker CCs (econ ramp 1.06-1.27x); the upper econ tranches over-priced the already-committed fleet and the model under-ran CC. fleet.cc_intermediate_plants routes the measured cohort to the new CC_INTERMEDIATE curve (econ 0.95-1.08x flat near-baseload incremental cost), keeping the physically-real duct-burner peak (2.25x) unchanged. LEVER 2 -- miso_pjm_border_anchor: the PJM neighbor price was anchored to PJM system-average LMP, which is pulled up by eastern load centres; constants.MISO_PJM_BORDER_HR_BY_YEAR re-anchors to the equal-weight mean of the three MISO-facing western PJM hubs (ComEd/AEP/ATSI), per-year ratio 0.981/0.956/0.936 (2023/24/25), deepening as eastern congestion widens. Both levers trace to measured inputs (CAMPD median CF; PJM zonal RT LMP), assign offer/price shapes, never pin output. Headline vs miso18: net-interchange duration RMSE 2024 1252->1051 MW, 2025 2037->1717 MW; total net-interchange |error| 23.5->20.5 TWh; gas |error| vs EIA-923 (3yr) 55.1->50.8 TWh. NOT-YET: residual gas-CC under-run 2023/24 (~-23/-20 TWh), 2025 dear-gas coal over-run (+14.2 TWh), and import under-run 2024/25 are open MODEL MISS items; exceptions ledger empty.
